mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz CLC 180 or 200 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement M271 engine for a CLC 180 or 200 petrol typically costs between £600 and £3,800 depending on the engine code and condition. Used units start from £600-£1,600, reconditioned from £1,200-£2,800, and fully rebuilt from £1,800-£3,800. A replacement motor of type 271.957 (similar family) costs on average £2,750 in good condition, with reconditioned units costing up to £3,124. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£900.

mainEntity.name: Does the CLC 180 or 200 petrol have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: All CLC 180 and 200 petrol engines use the M271 engine, which has a timing chain, not a belt. The M271 uses a single-row timing chain that is considered a wear item - failure typically occurs between 45,000-90,000 miles. The CLCs had the latest M271 Kompressor engine and the major issue on this engine is the timing chain stretching around/after 80k miles. A rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start is the classic warning sign.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a CLC 180 or 200 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M271-equipped CLC 180 and 200 petrol models, the most common symptom is a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start. Other signs include the check engine light (P0016 or P0017 codes), rough idle, loss of power, extended cranking, and hard starting. If the chain breaks, pistons meet valves and the motor is done. The M271 engine is an interference design - if the timing chain breaks or slips, valves and pistons hit and the engine is effectively junk.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz CLC 180 or 200 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and mileage. A CLC 180 or 200 petrol is typically worth £2,000-£5,000 - a rebuilt M271 engine (£2,000-£3,400) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. For lower-value examples, a targeted repair (timing chain, camshaft adjusters) may be more economical than a full replacement. The M271 engine can run 200,000 km+ reliably if addressed early.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CLC 180, CLC 200 Kompressor and CLC 200 CGI engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: All three use the M271 1.8-litre four-cylinder engine, but with different induction and injection systems. The CLC 180 Kompressor uses the M271.946 with an Eaton M45 supercharger, producing 143 hp. The CLC 200 Kompressor uses the M271.950 with the same supercharger but a higher-output tune, producing 184 hp. The CLC 200 CGI uses the M271.860 with direct injection (stratified-charged gasoline injection) instead of a supercharger, also producing 184 hp.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz CLC 180 / 200 petrol to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the CLC 180 and 200 petrol depends on the engine configuration. On Kompressor variants, timing chain stretch can cause cam timing drift, reducing power. On CGI variants, carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection can restrict airflow and cause power loss. Supercharger coupler wear can also cause performance issues on Kompressor cars. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz CLC 180 / 200 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The CLC 180 and 200 petrol badges formed the core of the Mercedes-Benz CLC petrol lineup throughout its 2008-2011 production run. All variants used the M271 1.8-litre four-cylinder engine, offered in three distinct forms: supercharged Kompressor variants for the CLC 180 and CLC 200, and a direct-injection CGI version for the CLC 200. The CL203 platform - a heavily updated version of the C-Class Sports Coupe - housed these engines with over 1,100 new components introduced for the CLC rebranding. The M271 engine family was introduced in 2002 as the successor to the M111 and predecessor to the M274.

milestones.description: M271.946, 1.8L supercharged petrol, 143 hp (105 kW) - CLC 180 Kompressor launch; Eaton M45 supercharger; 220 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 9.4 seconds
M271.950, 1.8L supercharged petrol, 184 hp (135 kW) - CLC 200 Kompressor launch; Eaton M45 supercharger; 250 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 8.6 seconds
M271.860, 1.8L direct-injection petrol (CGI), 184 hp (135 kW) - CLC 200 CGI launch; stratified-charged gasoline injection; improved fuel economy
CLC 160 BlueEFFICIENCY introduced with 1.6L M271.910 (129 hp); CLC 200 CGI continues
Production ends in June 2011; CLC petrol range discontinued

problems.h4: M271 Timing Chain Failure - Why the CLC 180 / 200 Petrol Rattles on Startup
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz CLC 180 and 200 petrol (M271.946, M271.950 and M271.860, 2008-2011)
problems.rootCause: The M271 uses a single-row timing chain that stretches over time, combined with a plastic tensioner guide that loses hydraulic pressure. The CLCs had the latest M271 Kompressor engine and the major issue on this engine is the timing chain stretching around/after 80k miles. The simplex cam chain can fail or round off the camshaft gears so the timing is out. Cold starts produce a distinctive rattle as the chain slaps against the timing cover. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, causing valve-to-piston contact and complete engine destruction.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioner, guides, and camshaft sprockets. Labour-intensive (8-10 hours)
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000+ miles. Only viable before chain jumps. Essential preventative maintenance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioner, guides, and both camshaft adjusters
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000+ miles. Recommended if camshaft adjuster wear is also present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt M271 with upgraded timing components, new oil pump, and bench testing
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or engine has suffered valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical CLC 180 or 200 petrol is worth £2,000-£5,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £3,500, a preventative timing chain replacement (£800-£1,200) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M271 with warranty (£2,000-£3,400) offers peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold starts - especially between 45,000 and 90,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist (£800-£1,200) saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. The M271 Kompressor timing chain can let go without warning, while the CGI version typically gives adequate warning. Once the chain jumps, piston-to-valve contact is almost certain and engine replacement becomes the only viable option.

problems.h4: M271 Camshaft Adjuster Failure - The VVT Rattle That Won't Quit
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz CLC 180 and 200 petrol (M271.946 and M271.950, 2008-2011)
problems.rootCause: The M271's camshaft adjusters (VVT phasers) rely on oil pressure to vary cam timing. Internally, the locking mechanism can wear - the plates have a groove worn in them by the pin. This causes a loud rattling noise from the top of the engine that persists beyond the initial cold start - distinct from chain tensioner rattle. Fault codes P0016, P0017, or P0025 confirm the issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of one or both camshaft adjusters, timing chain, tensioner, and guides
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000+ miles. Often done alongside timing chain replacement

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt M271 with new adjusters, upgraded timing components, and full warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if adjuster failure has caused valve timing errors leading to piston contact

problems.recommendation: If your M271 petrol CLC rattles constantly from the top end - not just at cold start - have a specialist diagnose the adjusters. Replacing them alongside the timing chain is cost-effective labour-wise as the timing cover is already off. Between 45K and 90K miles on the M271 cam adjusters, the plates have a groove worn in them by the pin. On a well-maintained CLC 180 or 200 Kompressor, this repair gives you another 60,000+ miles of reliable service.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for M271 camshaft adjuster replacement for your CLC 180 / 200 petrol

problems.group: M271 CGI Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
problems.h4: M271 CGI Intake Valve Carbon Buildup - Direct Injection Deposits (CLC 200 CGI)
problems.rootCause: On M271 engines with CGI direct injection, soot and carbon deposits often build up on the intake valves and in the intake tract. Because fuel is injected directly into the cylinder rather than washing over the intake valves, carbon accumulates on the valve stems and seats. Symptoms include rough idling, power loss, hesitation on acceleration, and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Intake Valve Carbon Cleaning (Walnut Blasting)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, blast valves with walnut media
repairOptions.longevity: Viable; restores performance and fuel economy

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt M271 CGI engine
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with cleaned intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Only if carbon buildup has caused significant valve damage

problems.recommendation: If your CLC 200 CGI feels sluggish or has reduced fuel economy, carbon cleaning is often the solution. Regular motorway driving helps reduce carbon buildup, but the design will still cause carbon build up regardless of fuel quality. A £350-£600 specialist clean is far cheaper than a £2,200 engine replacement. The M271 engine can run 200,000 km+ reliably if addressed early.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for M271 CGI carbon cleaning and engine replacement for your CLC 200 CGI

problems.h4: M271 Supercharger Coupler Wear - Kompressor Rattle and Whine
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz CLC 180 and 200 Kompressor (M271.946 and M271.950, 2008-2011)
problems.rootCause: The Eaton M45 supercharger uses a coupler that connects the drive pulley to the supercharger rotor. Over time, the coupler wears, producing a rattling or whining noise from the front of the engine that changes with engine speed. Catalytic converters and superchargers are usually good for 100K miles, then they are more prone to failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace supercharger coupler, inspect oil level
Full supercharger rebuild with new bearings and coupler
repairOptions.longevity: Required if bearings are also worn
Only if supercharger failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the front of the engine that changes with engine speed, have the supercharger coupler inspected. A £150-£350 specialist coupler replacement is significantly cheaper than a full supercharger rebuild or engine replacement. The Kompressor version of the M271 fails without warning after one fatal death rattle.
